A function in a `$:` statement is created again whenever what the statement reads changes, though a plain `const` would do. The rule looks at components that are not in runes mode.

With ESLint 10, eslint-plugin-svelte's rule throws when it reports, because its suggestion calls `sourceCode.isSpaceBetweenTokens`, which ESLint 10 removed. Bun does the same, so with ESLint 10 such a component ends the run. With an older ESLint the rule reports and suggests `const`.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  { rules: { "svelte/no-reactive-functions": "error" } },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}

```svelte
<script>
  $: format = (value) => value.toFixed(2);
</script>
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}

```svelte
<script>
  const format = (value) => value.toFixed(2);
</script>
```
